claims.statement: Installed PV and battery assets create current paid installation events and an installed base requiring monitoring, warranty administration and potential maintenance; the source confirms connected-and-paid assets but not maintenance spending.
The family installer relationship offers a realistic, nonexclusive route to test customer-consented renewal offers without transferring its customer book.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Owner of a renewable installer or service department
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: A revenue-share renewal rail aligns fees to collected service revenue and can coordinate multiple equipment warranties; CRM reminders alone do not provide the collection workflow.
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The prospective business would own installer subscription or revenue-share contracts; installers retain all homeowner relationships.
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Family installer pilot followed by white-label offers through equipment distributors.

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Assumption: 2,000-4,000 PLN per installer through direct sales; unknown until pilots.
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Platform fee prepaid monthly and revenue share collected when homeowner pays.
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 60-75% after messaging, payment and service coordination.
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Initial data-cleaning and campaign setup estimated at 20-40 hours per installer.
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Consent management, processor agreements, accounting and insurance estimated at 4,000 PLN monthly after 20 customers.
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Monthly platform fee plus 8-15% of collected maintenance-plan revenue.
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: SMS, payment processing, support and optional contracted technician dispatch.

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Installer CRMs and equipment distributors may bundle reminders; revenue-linked pricing and cross-brand service records provide resistance.
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Homeowner pays for a maintenance visit or annual care plan; the installer loses repeat revenue when installed-base customers are not contacted.
commercial_mechanics.payer: Installer pays platform fees; homeowner funds the underlying service event.
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Installer has more than 500 installed systems but little repeat-service revenue.
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual platform renewal tied to collected maintenance revenue.

contrary_evidence: Residential PV systems may require little paid preventive maintenance.
The cited subsidy material proves installed assets, not demand for annual plans.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Existing informal family operating relationship for voluntary service-workflow testing; any customer outreach requires installer authorization and valid customer consent.
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Recruit another installer and run opt-in campaigns from newly completed installations rather than importing legacy customer data.
critical_control_point.current_owner: Each installer owns its customer contracts and service history.
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The prospective business would own installer subscription or revenue-share contracts; installers retain all homeowner relationships.
critical_control_point.duration: Ongoing relationship with no fixed term.
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Family-business access can validate workflow and economics, but gives no automatic right to homeowner data.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: The founder would control campaign logic, payment routing and installer contracts if launched.
critical_control_point.renewal: Mutual-consent operating access; proposed commercial contracts would define annual renewal.
critical_control_point.subject: Renewable installer service-renewal workflow

economics.acquisition_route: Run an opt-in cohort on new installations, prove service conversion, then sell to installers with 500-5,000 assets.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 100 installers averaging 2,500 PLN platform MRR plus 15,000 PLN annual revenue share yields about 4.5M PLN revenue; at 25% owner earnings and 4x value, an 80% stake could pass 5M PLN in years 6-8. Conversion and service frequency remain unknown.
economics.founder_time: 15 hours weekly for pilot; outsource campaign operations after ten installers.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Platform and revenue-share income less messaging, payments and direct support; target 65%.
economics.payback: Installer should recover fees from 5-10 incremental service plans monthly; target founder CAC payback under six months.
economics.pricing: 750-2,500 PLN monthly plus 8-15% of collected service revenue.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Installed-base growth and annual warranty or inspection cycles support repeat usage.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned response and asset-service benchmarks improve renewal timing.
fingerprint.customer: Residential renewable installers with substantial installed bases.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label installer channel and equipment-distributor referrals.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Managed renewal rail with platform fee and revenue share.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer pays platform fee; homeowner payment for service generates shared revenue.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A large dormant installed base and weak repeat-service revenue.

founder_fit: Family installer offers legally usable workflow access
Quantitative campaign optimization suits the founder
Can begin part-time with opt-in records
Capital need is below available 100,000 PLN
risks: Consent and data-processing mistakes could create GDPR exposure.
Installer service capacity may constrain fulfilled demand.

structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: replaceable access to installer renewal workflow
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: installers or technicians fulfilling booked service

structure.control_point: Opt-in service renewal and payment event
structure.critical_dependency: Installer service capacity and homeowner conversion

thesis: Turn renewable installers' dormant installed bases into recurring service revenue through a consented renewal and payment rail.
title: Installer Maintenance Renewal Rail
uncertainties: Installer capacity and acceptable revenue share
